According to Mark Gurman's latest "Power On" newsletter, Apple is working to turn its upcoming non-AR smart glasses into another health and fitness platform — though these features are not expected to debut alongside the first-generation model next year.

According to his report, Apple previously attempted to turn the Vision Pro into a health platform. The company reportedly developed a version of its Fitness+ app that could run on the headset, allowing users to watch workout videos, track their movements, and complete Move ring goals inside Apple's first spatial computing device.

That version was originally planned to include some special posture-tracking analytics features to set it apart from iPad or Apple TV. However, due to the headset being too heavy, the company ultimately abandoned the plans:

However, the company is now reimagining a similar concept for its upcoming smart glasses — though since glasses themselves have no display screen, the design has to be adjusted accordingly.

Fitness features on the smart glasses

Apple's exact plans for the smart glasses remain unclear, but what is certain is that the company is actively recruiting related talent. The report quoted as follows:

The first thing that came to mind was the Workout Buddy feature Apple Watch launched last year, paired with heart rate sensors that might be built into the glasses — similar to the design first adopted in the AirPods Pro 3. This setup has real potential to make the glasses a practical companion for runners.

The cameras on the glasses could also play a role during various activities, letting the system identify whether the user's movements are correct and in turn help improve fitness performance.

What solution Apple ultimately delivers remains to be seen. As mentioned at the outset, these features are not expected to appear on the first-generation model — so it may take another two years before we get a glimpse of Apple's full blueprint.
